title: IndicVisionBench: Benchmarking Cultural and Multilingual Understanding in VLMs
claim: A benchmark is built by routing diverse image sources through quality checks into distinct task tracks, each shown with a concrete example.
layout: 2 tiers: top left-to-right flow with counts, bottom three example panels
description: The top half is a left-to-right data collection flowchart. Gray dashed boxes on the left hold the image sources: crowd sourcing, internet images and Wikisource. Arrows carry them through an image filter, VLM-based generation, a yellow Quality Check zone (correction, OCR quality filter), LLM translation and human correction. Image counts (615, 3502, 1113, 106, 1007, 4117, 876) label the arrows. The flow ends in a blue-gray IndicVisionBench box with colored track boxes: IVB-MMT, IVB-VQA-Parallel, IVB-VQA-Indic, IVB-VQA-EN and IVB-OCR. Small flat icons mark each stage. The bottom half has three dashed panels, one each for VQA, MMT and OCR. Each panel pairs a photo or document image (a red fort, ragi mudde with soup, Punjabi text) with rounded bubbles of question, translation or ground-truth text in Indic scripts.
caption: IndicVisionBench (IVB) pipeline and 3 tracks. Top panel illustrates our image collection pipeline for 10 Indian languages, showing the number of images at each step, with human quality checks applied throughout. We also present sample outputs for the three tracks: VQA (Visual Question Answering) in English, MMT (Multimodal Machine Translation) in Telugu, and OCR (Optical Character Recognition) in Punjabi. Further details are provided in Section [ref].
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive generalization across multimodal tasks, yet most evaluation benchmarks remain Western-centric, leaving open questions about their performance in culturally diverse and multilingual settings. To address this gap, we introduce IndicVisionBench, the first large-scale benchmark centered on the Indian subcontinent. Covering English and 10 Indian languages, our benchmark spans 3 multimodal tasks, including Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Multimodal Machine Translation (MMT), and Visual Question Answering (VQA), covering 6 kinds of question types. Our final benchmark consists of a total of ~5K images and 37K+ QA pairs across 13 culturally grounded topics. In addition, we release a paired parallel corpus of annotations across 10 Indic languages, creating a unique resource for analyzing cultural and linguistic biases in VLMs. We evaluate a broad spectrum of 8 models, from proprietary closed-source systems to open-weights medium and large-scale models. Our experiments reveal substantial performance gaps, underscoring the limitations of current VLMs in culturally diverse contexts. By centering cultural diversity and multilinguality, IndicVisionBench establishes a reproducible evaluation framework that paves the way for more inclusive multimodal research.
